rounded by  the  government  troops,  and  that  he  would  not  be  able  to 
join  that  chief,  Charles  resolved  to  leave  it  immediately.  To  lessen

took  leave  of  Borodale  and  his  son* in-law,  and  attended  by  Glenaladale,

in  the  French  service,  and  John  Macdonald  junior,  Borodale’s  son,

reached  the  summit  of  a hill,  called  Scoorvuy,  at  the  eastern  ex- 
tremity of  Arisaig.  Here  they  rested  and  took  some  refreshment,

Borodale,  who  had  proceeded  to  Glen  Morar  in  advance  of  the  party 
to  procure  some  necessaries,  received  information,  on  his  arrival  there, 
that  some  men-of-war  with  troops  on  board,  under  General  Campbell, 
had  anchored  in  Loch  Nevis.  He  thereupon  despatched  two  men  to 
Loch  Nevis,  by  way  of  Loch  Morar,  to  observe  General  Campbell’s 
motions,  and  having  received  farther  intelligence,  that  Captain  Scott  had 
arrived  with  a party  in  the  lower  part  of  Arisaig,  he  returned  to 
Charles,  and  communicated  to  him  the  information  he  had  received.

he  entertained  him  in  the  best  manner  he  could  for  three  days,  and  in 
the  meantime,  Charles  despatched  John  Macdonald,  junior,  one  of  Boro- 
dale’s  sons,  with  a letter  to  Alexander  Macdonald  of  Glenaladale,  who 
had  been  in  his  service  as  Major  of  the  Clanranald  regiment.f  Receiv-
